title: Canary release pinning notes - Sophia Lee
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for pinning strategy during the upcoming canary (v2.3.0 -> v2.4.0).
- Target: low-risk rollout for model-serving runtime changes (batching + KV cache improvement) plus small API surface tweak.
- Goal: detect regressions early, keep user impact ~0, enable fast rollback.

Assumptions:
- New image: redwood/runtime:v2.4.0-canary (build 2026-02-17).
- Backwards-compatible API; config flag ENABLE_CACHE_OPT defaults to false in prod until pinned.
- Observability: per-route latency, 95/99 p50/ p95 p99, error rate (5xx, model errors), token cost delta, e2e synthetic tests.

Pinning rules (draft):
- Two independent dimensions:
  1) Traffic percent pin to new image (route-level): 0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%
  2) Feature flag for cache optimizations (global flag): off -> staged on for canary hosts -> on for all canary traffic -> full roll
- Enforce minimum dwell time between steps: at least 30m at 1% and 2h at 5%+, unless all signals good earlier.
- Manual approval required to jump >20%.

Rollout checklist (quick):
- Pre-rollout (before any traffic)
  - [ ] Smoke e2e test run against v2.4.0-canary (runbook: /runbooks/canary-smoke)
  - [ ] Load baseline metrics captured (last 24h) for affected routes
  - [ ] Notify #releases + rotations on-call (Maya)
  - [ ] Create release rollout ticket JIRA-RELEASE-789 and link artifacts

- Canary steps:
  - [ ] Deploy v2.4.0-canary to canary pool (k8s label: rollout=canary)
  - [ ] Pin 1% traffic to canary; enable logging at debug for canary requests (short TTL)
  - [ ] After 30m: check signals (see Monitoring Signals) -> if OK, move to 5%
  - [ ] At 5%: run synthetic regen and a small sample of production prompts for quality eval (Priya/QA)
  - [ ] After 2h at 5% and green: 20% -> wait 4h -> 50% (manual) -> 100%

Monitoring Signals (primary):
- Latency: p95 increase > 15% from baseline -> hold/rollback
- Error rate (5xx) absolute > 0.5% or relative > 2x baseline -> rollback
- Model inference failures (KV misses leading to >5% token error) -> rollback
- Cost: token/unit cost delta > 10% -> investigate (expected small increase due to caching warmups)
- User-facing regressions detected by Prod QA (false positives, hallucinations) -> immediate rollback
- Synthetic tests: any failing test for >2 consecutive runs -> hold

Rollback criteria / immediate abort:
- Any of the above thresholds breached in 15m window
- Canary pool OOM/crashloop for >2 pods in 10m
- Observed increase in support tickets for endpoint X

Observability playbook (quick checks):
- Dashboards: releases -> model-serving -> route-<A/B/C> (p50/p95/p99, errors)
- Logs: search for "kv_cache_error", "inference_timeout", "OOM" + pod name redwood-runtime-canary
- Tracing: check tail latency spikes correlating with backend calls (redis/kv-store)
- A/B diff: sample outputs for a set of 50 prompts (compare v2.3.0 baseline vs canary)

Runtime commands (helpers):
- Pin traffic (feature flag system):
  - curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/rollouts -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","image":"redwood/runtime:v2.4.0-canary","percent":5}'  # replace with CLI helper
- Kubernetes: kubectl --context prod apply -f deploy/canary-deployment.yaml -l rollout=canary
- Feature flag toggle (LaunchDarkly): ldctl set cache_opt true --env production --scope canary_hosts

Notes / open questions (TODO):
- Q: Should we use IP-based sampling or header-based for precise user subset? Header-based easier for QA but misses real-user diversity.
- Q: How to handle customers on dedicated pools? Need explicit communication; make sure we don't pin to Dedicated clusters by mistake (exclude by label).
- Need to confirm canary pool size >= 10 pods to get meaningful p95 metrics under bursty load. Action: ask infra (Noah) to validate.
- Consider short-circuit for small-but-severe regressions: auto-rollback if token-cost delta > 50% in 15m (protect billing).

Post-roll notes (to capture during rollout):
- timestamp, step, pre/post metrics snapshot, decision (go/hold/rollback), rationale, who approved. Keep in ticket comments.

Links/references (quick):
- Confluence runbook: CONF-RELEASE-42 (runbooks/canary-smoke)
- JIRA: JIRA-RELEASE-789
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/234

Quick timeline sketch (ideal):
- T0: deploy canary image -> 1%
- T0+30m: check -> 5%
- T0+2h: check -> 20% (manual approval)
- T0+6h: 50% (manual)
- T0+12-24h: 100%

Notes to self (scratch):
- If we see small latency bump that drops after cache warms, annotate and keep going. If persistent, rollback.
- Keep debug logs at limited retention (10m) to avoid cost explosion.
- Ping Maya after first 1% dwell to verify smoke looks good.

---
Bottom line: conservative, manual gate at 20%+, short dwell at low %s, strong observability checks. Will refine after dry run with Maya/Noah.
